title: Downtown Warehouse Homicide
excerpt: Multiple blood stain patterns identified at warehouse crime scene. Spatter analysis confirmed blunt force trauma consistent with autopsy findings.
findings: Blood spatter consistent with blunt force impact at 45° angle
Luminol revealed extensive cleanup attempts in 3 zones
Victim and suspect DNA both present – mixed profile separated
Cast-off pattern on ceiling confirmed weapon trajectory
summary: Warehouse homicide with extensive blood evidence. Spatter analysis revealed blunt force trauma mechanism. Luminol detected cleaned blood in 3 areas. DNA STR profiling matched suspect with 16/16 loci.
resolution: Suspect convicted. Blood evidence was primary forensic link tying suspect to the scene and the weapon used.

title: Riverfront Assault Investigation
excerpt: Victim sustained lacerations. Blood trail analysis mapped suspect's movement through the scene and identified secondary transfer evidence.
findings: Passive drip trail established movement from point of assault to exit
Secondary transfer on door handle matched suspect's ABO type
Directionality of drops confirmed victim's path toward medical help
Fabric impression transfer consistent with assailant's clothing
summary: Assault near the riverfront with clear blood trail documenting victim and suspect movement. ABO typing differentiated two contributors. Transfer evidence on surfaces traced suspect's escape route.
resolution: Investigation ongoing. Suspect identified via transfer blood evidence on exit door handle.

title: Cold Case #447 – Suburb Residence
excerpt: Re-examination of preserved blood samples using modern STR analysis. New DNA profiles generated from degraded evidence previously deemed inconclusive.
findings: Original 1992 analysis limited to ABO blood grouping only
Modern STR profiling recovered 12 of 16 loci from degraded stains
New partial profile entered into CODIS – pending hit notification
Secondary sample from fabric yielded additional 4 loci for composite
summary: Cold case reopened with advanced STR profiling applied to 30+ year old preserved blood evidence. Partial DNA profile generated and submitted to national database.
resolution: Under review. Awaiting CODIS database match results from newly generated STR profile.

title: Nightclub Altercation – DNA Match
excerpt: DNA profiling of blood evidence from broken glass fragments linked suspect to aggravated assault. Full STR match confirmed identity.
findings: Blood on broken glass edges matched suspect's DNA profile exactly
AB+ blood type rare enough to narrow suspect pool immediately
CODIS search returned positive match to previously convicted individual
Glass fragment trajectory analysis consistent with aggressive strike
summary: Nightclub assault case solved through DNA profiling of blood found on broken glass. Full STR match linked suspect who was already in CODIS from prior conviction.
resolution: Suspect arrested and charged. DNA evidence from glass fragments served as conclusive forensic link.

title: Vehicle Collision – Blood Evidence
excerpt: Suspected hit-and-run with blood evidence found on vehicle bumper. Serological analysis matched victim's blood type and DNA to evidence on car.
findings: Blood spatter on bumper consistent with pedestrian impact velocity
O- blood type matched victim's hospital records
DNA STR from bumper sample: 14/16 loci match to victim
Embedded fabric fibers matched victim's clothing material
summary: Hit-and-run investigation with blood evidence recovered from suspect vehicle. Serological and DNA analysis confirmed victim contact. Fabric fiber analysis provided supplementary evidence.
resolution: Active investigation. Vehicle owner identified; awaiting suspect interview and formal charges.

title: Residential Break-In – Blood on Entry Point
excerpt: Suspect cut themselves on broken window during forced entry. Blood drops on window sill and floor provided DNA profile leading to identification.
findings: Passive blood drops on window sill indicated suspect's hand injury
Directional analysis of floor drops mapped suspect's path through residence
A+ blood type not matching any residents – confirmed as intruder's
CODIS database returned match to known offender within 48 hours
summary: Residential burglary solved through suspect's own blood left at point of forced entry. Directional drop analysis traced movement inside. CODIS match identified repeat offender.
resolution: Suspect apprehended based on CODIS DNA match. Convicted of aggravated burglary with assault.

title: Park Stabbing Incident
excerpt: Multiple victims in park stabbing. Blood from the weapon and scene collected for serological differentiation of contributors.
findings: Kitchen knife yielded blood from 3 different contributors (A+, B-, O+)
Scene stains differentiated into 4 distinct profiles using ABO+Rh
Fatal victim (B-) had blood concentrated at primary attack zone
Suspect's blood (A+) found on knife handle – self-inflicted cut
summary: Complex park stabbing with multiple victims requiring careful serological differentiation. Four unique blood profiles separated through ABO and Rh typing combined with spatial analysis.
resolution: Under judicial review. Blood evidence differentiation critical to establishing assault sequence and identifying the primary attacker.

title: Forensic Lab QC – Contamination Audit
excerpt: Internal quality control audit uncovered cross-contamination in batch processing. AB- control sample detected in unrelated case evidence.
findings: AB- control DNA detected in 3 unrelated case samples
Root cause traced to improper pipette tip change between samples
All affected cases re-processed with new evidence collection
Lab protocol updated with mandatory dual-operator verification
summary: Quality control audit revealed laboratory cross-contamination affecting 3 cases. Root cause analysis identified procedural failure. All affected evidence re-processed and new protocols implemented.
resolution: Contamination resolved. Lab procedures updated with dual verification. Affected case evidence re-analyzed with clean results.
